clue.text: Return to previous arrangement for fairground ride

definitions.meaning: to change things back to how they were before
a roller coaster with steep ups and downs

explanation.surface: Someone restores an old layout to make room for a fairground attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch back is to revert to an earlier setting, and a switchback is also a roller coaster at a funfair.

clue.text: Stripteaser responsible for man losing his head

definitions.meaning: a woman who performs a dance shedding clothes, here the biblical dance of the seven veils

definitions.text: responsible for man losing his head
definitions.meaning: the person whose request led to John the Baptist's beheading

explanation.surface: A burlesque dancer drives some poor fellow to distraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing his head' reads as infatuation, but it is literal: in the Gospel story the dancer asked Herod for the head of John the Baptist.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Herod's stepdaughter danced the dance of the seven veils and demanded the Baptist's head as her reward.

clue.text: High-flier brought down after exposure in sun

definitions.text: High-flier brought down after exposure in sun

parts.words: High-flier brought down after exposure in sun
parts.note: reads like an ambitious person ruined by publicity, but describes the Greek myth of the boy whose wax wings melted when he flew too near the sun

explanation.surface: A rising star falls from grace after too much time in the limelight.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Daedalus's son flew with wings of wax and feathers, rose too close to the sun, and fell into the sea.

clue.text: Walk like our monarchy

definitions.meaning: a stroll taken for the sake of one's health
describing a monarchy limited by a constitution, as Britain's is

explanation.surface: A remark comparing a stroll to the British crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A constitutional is a health-giving stroll, and Britain's is a constitutional monarchy whose powers are fixed by law.

clue.text: Where to get train fare

parts.note: fare looks like the price of a ticket, but it means food served on board a train

explanation.surface: A traveller asks where to buy a rail ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway carriage serving snacks and drinks is where passengers obtain food during the journey.

clue.text: What's on board old vessel south of cape?

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece below another comes after it, so the ship follows the cape

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
the Argo was the ancient ship of Jason and the Argonauts

explanation.surface: A question about what was carried aboard an ancient ship sailing below a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods loaded on a ship for transport are its freight.

clue.text: A stud manager

definitions.meaning: a raised ornamental knob, as on a shield or ceiling
the person in charge at work

explanation.surface: A breeding farm's horse is put in charge of the business.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a decorative raised knob like a stud, and also the employer who gives the orders.

clue.text: Perform better? Not in band

parts.note: someone not in is out
a strip is a narrow band of material

explanation.surface: A musician wonders whether leaving the group would improve their playing.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip rivals is to surpass or outdo them.

clue.text: Military duty, thus, that's about access at front of garrison

indicators.note: one piece goes around the others, so the word for thus wraps them

parts.note: so means thus, in that way
an entry is a way in, an access

indicators.note: only the opening letter of garrison is used

explanation.surface: A soldier's posting described as being about guarding the gateway to a fort.
explanation.walkthrough: Sentry-go is an old army term for a guard's spell of duty; 'that's' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentry-go is the duty of a soldier on guard patrol.

clue.text: Worthless, or noble and free

parts.note: good in the sense of virtuous, noble
something got for nothing costs nothing, is free

explanation.surface: Someone is weighed up as either useless or a generous free spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: An idle, useless person is called a ne'er-do-well, of no value at all.

clue.text: Grasp short line attached to net

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line
to net money is to earn it as profit

explanation.surface: A fisherman ties a short line to his net to grab hold of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp a subject is to come to understand it, to acquire knowledge.

clue.text: Overlooked pro achieved 50% of score

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
got means obtained or achieved
a score is twenty, and half of it is ten

explanation.surface: A professional who only managed half marks gets passed over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forgotten has been neglected or missed, not remembered.

clue.text: North American lawman put up with 25

parts.note: to mount a picture or display is to put it up
the answer to 25 across is the Latin phrase meaning namely, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A sheriff is installed alongside a numbered colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: The '25' is a cross-reference to 25 across, whose Latin phrase is usually shortened to IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police is a police officer in Canada.

clue.text: Veteran of sort led badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A veteran sort of person led poorly in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: An elderly person, someone advanced in years, is an old-timer.

clue.text: Standard royalty brother divides, managing shares, say

indicators.note: a piece splitting another goes between its parts, so the sibling sits between the first two

parts.note: stock as an adjective means standard, regular
a king is royalty

explanation.surface: A sibling causes a rift in the royal family over regular business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the definition as an example of the trade rather than a full synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying and selling securities on behalf of clients is the trade of a broker on the stock market.

clue.text: Way in which London runners maintained order?

definitions.text: Way in which London runners maintained order?

parts.words: Way in which London runners maintained order?
parts.note: way looks like a method, but means a street; the runners were London's early police force named after the magistrates' court there

explanation.surface: A question about how marathoners in the capital kept in line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bow Street Runners were London's first professional police force, founded in the 18th century at the magistrates' court on that street.
explanation.definitionFit: The early police officers known as Runners were based at the magistrates' office on this London thoroughfare.

clue.text: Put squeeze on revolutionary newspapers

parts.note: Com. is an abbreviation for Communist, a revolutionary
the press means newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: A radical leans on the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: To compress something is to squash it into less space by pressure.

clue.text: Oddly, erect arch outside? Not in the open

indicators.note: one piece sits on the outside of another, enclosing it

parts.note: arch means knowing, sly

indicators.note: the word erect is treated oddly, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Strangely, someone has built an archway outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like a call for odd letters, but here it signals an anagram, making ECRET.
explanation.definitionFit: Done covertly, without others knowing, is the opposite of done openly.

clue.text: Defeating husband in public argument

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the others, so the husband sits within them

parts.note: overt means open, public
a rowing is a quarrel or argument

explanation.surface: A husband is beaten in a very public quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Toppling or bringing down a ruler or regime is to beat it.

clue.text: International force supported by everyone else in strife

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece below holds up the one above, so the peacekeepers come first

parts.note: the UN provides international peacekeeping forces
the rest means everyone else

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers are backed by the rest of the world in a conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrest is disturbance and turmoil, a state of conflict.

clue.text: Loyal editor didn't scoff

parts.note: fast means firm, loyal, as in fast friends

explanation.surface: A faithful editor refused to mock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoff' looks like jeer, but here means eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has fasted has gone without food, has not eaten.

clue.text: Legislative assembly restricted our part of house

parts.note: parliament cut short gives the abbreviation Parl.

explanation.surface: The legislature limited our part of the building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of house' looks parliamentary, after the assembly, but means a room in a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A parlour is a sitting room in a private home.

clue.text: Indian dish with yoghurt, as correspondent reported

indicators.note: said out loud, so the word for correspondent is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a correspondent is a writer, of letters or articles

explanation.surface: A journalist describes a South Asian yoghurt dish.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, writer sounds like this dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is a cooling side dish of yoghurt mixed with cucumber or herbs, served with curry.

clue.text: Ain't it strange a queen falling in love with a donkey!

definitions.text: queen falling in love with a donkey

indicators.note: strange letters are oddly arranged, so these words are mixed up

explanation.surface: An exclamation at the oddity of a queen besotted with an ass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges AINTIT to TITANI. In A Midsummer Night's Dream, the fairy queen is bewitched into loving Bottom, who wears an ass's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's fairy queen in A Midsummer Night's Dream dotes on Bottom after he is transformed into an ass.

clue.text: River and sea unite, blended in such a place

indicators.note: things blended are mixed together, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fresh and salt water mingle where a river meets the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blended' rearranges R plus SEAUNITE. 'Such a place' points back to the surface: where river and sea meet is an estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: Estuarine describes what lives or lies in a tidal river mouth, the very spot the surface pictures.

clue.text: A day in Rome, with little time, namely, for Romans

parts.note: the ides was a fixed day in the Roman calendar, mid-month
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A Roman date is pinned down, with little time to spare.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means that is, and is used to introduce a clarification.

clue.text: Channel east of Scottish island

parts.note: Sky is a British television channel

explanation.surface: A sea channel lies to the east of a Scottish isle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' suggests a sea strait but is the British TV broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is the largest island of the Inner Hebrides, off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Players I kept in school and told off

parts.note: the cast is the set of actors in a play
a pupil gated is confined to school as punishment

explanation.surface: Actors kept me in detention and scolded me.
explanation.walkthrough: Being gated is British school and college slang for being confined to the premises as punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to reprimand severely, to scold.
